newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures mixed, yen, marks up sharply.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures mixed, yen, marks up sharply.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed in early trade, as yen and marks rose on worries about the fate of European monetary union (EMU) after France requested a "period of reflection" on the EMU budget stability pact.
"You can kiss EMU good-bye," one currency futures trader said.

France asked its European Union partners for a period of consultation with its National Assembly over the EMU stability pact. Later French finance minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn confirmed to a news conference that the stability pact had not been agreed on Monday.
Strauss-Kahn said the new French government would need at least a week to consider the budget accord.

Some futures traders were fearful that a week of consideration by the new French government could lead to a collapse of the EMU. They said an unwinding of short cash marks on the crosses helped support September marks.
September is lead contract month for all IMM currency futures.
Strauss-Kahn noted there would be further discussion with France's EU partners in the coming days, particularly at the Franco-German summit on Friday.
September marks traded slightly above the GLOBEX high of $0.5880, but remained within 2-1/4-month ranges.
It was the September yen contract, however, that posted the sharpest price swing overnight. EMU jitters helped September yen widen its gains to $0.000211 on GLOBEX.

Earlier in the overnight session, September yen rose to $0.009060, above the 5-3/4-month high of $0.009050, on fears of renewed trade friction between the U.S. and Japan ahead of the Group of Seven meeting on June 20-22 in Denver.
There were also ideas that the U.S.-Japan interest rate differential that has benefited the dollar and U.S. assets in recent months may be narrowing.

However, comments from several Japanese officials limited buying in yen futures, traders said. Japanese vice minister of International Trade and Industry Tsutomu Makino said the recent rise in the yen against the dollar is excessive.

Meanwhile, September Canadian dollars weakened in sympathy with the dollar. Traders also cited concerns about Canada's political situation. September Canadian dollars fell to $0.7260, through the 3-1/2-week settlement low of $0.7279.
Traders said Swiss franc futures were supported after Swiss voters agreed to keep arms exports.

At 0823 CDT/1323 GMT, September yen was up $0.000171 at $0.009020, marks were up $0.0056 at $0.5889, Swiss francs were $0.0079 higher at $0.7053, sterling was up $0.0014 at $1.63, Canadian dollars were down $0.0007 at $0.7272, Australian dollars were $0.0016 lower at $0.7617 and Mexican pesos were off $0.000175 at $0.119375.
